one_month_reasoning: No company catalyst in the window: Qualcomm reported fiscal Q4 exactly 38 days after fiscal year-end in FY23 (Nov 1), FY24 (Nov 6) and FY25 (Nov 5, source 20); FY26 ended Sep 27, so the print is most likely Wed Nov 4, after Oct 30 (I drop round 1's small allowance for an Oct 29 print). In-window drivers are peer read-throughs (TSMC mid-Oct, Samsung/SK hynix/Apple late Oct: memory pricing and handset demand) and the Oct 27-28 FOMC after the Fed's confirmed Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (source 22). None of these has a clear expected sign for QCOM. The stock fell ~9% in the last week of September after a big run; short-horizon reversal and continued de-risking into the print roughly offset. So I stay essentially symmetric around spot (median ~$184.8) with a ~12% monthly core sigma (between the long-run 39% and recent ~49% annualised vol, /sqrt(12)) plus a 15% weight on a 20% sigma tail for news shocks, which is a little tighter at the tails than round 1 now that earnings is clearly outside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend on one consistent non-GAAP basis: (a) FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$11.2 x 16x = $179 (40%); (b) base-rate multiple anchor, FY27 non-GAAP EPS $10.0 x 15.8x (5-year median trailing non-GAAP P/E 13.8x plus 2 turns for the non-handset mix) = $158 (25%); (c) normalized FCF ~$10.5/share in FY28 at a 5.75% yield = $183 (35%). Weighted ~$175.

inputs_detail.derivation: Company-basis non-GAAP FY27 consensus ~$10.20 (Yahoo, 34 analysts, per supervisor fact-check); trimmed ~2% because revisions are still falling and Q4 FY26 guide ($2.05-2.25) sits well below year-ago Q1 ($3.50).

Base rate: the last post-trough recovery year (FY23 $8.43 -> FY24 $10.22) grew +21%; haircut to ~12% because IDC still sees 2027 handset units falling, custom silicon carries a gross-margin drag, and the ~$5B FY27 data-center guide is not yet proven (first revenue Dec quarter).

Forward P/E on realized next-year non-GAAP EPS at fiscal year-ends: Sep-22 $112.98/$8.43 = 13.4x, Sep-23 $111.06/$10.22 = 10.9x, Sep-24 $170.05/$12.03 = 14.1x, Sep-25 $166.36/~$10.5 = 15.8x (mean ~13.6x). Today ~18x on $10.2. Use 16x: above the handset-era mean for the data-center/auto mix, below today's multiple because estimates are still being cut.

inputs_detail.derivation: 9M FY26 OCF $8.4B less capex $1.6B, add back the one-off $1.8B inventory build, annualized ~$11B; take ~$10.5B (supervisor fact-check range $10-11B). The $5.55B tax line is not added back (it offsets a non-cash valuation-allowance release).
Q3 diluted 1,069M + 17.8M Modular shares issued Jul 28 (after quarter-end) less ~7-8M/qtr buybacks; Amazon warrant adds only ~0.5M net shares on the treasury method.

FY25 buybacks+dividends of ~$12.6B on a ~$180B market cap implied ~6-7% cash returns in the handset era; a slightly lower 5.75% credits the growth mix but keeps SBC (~$3.4B/yr, not deducted) in mind. FY28 FCF/share ~$10.5 (+7%) / 5.75% = $183.

bear.story: Memory-driven Android slump runs through 2027, Apple modem exit completes with the Sep-2027 iPhones, and the data-center ramp slips (first Amazon revenue small, few warrant tranches vest). FY28 EPS ~$9.5 at ~12.5x, near the FY23 trough multiple (10.9x forward) and the 52-week low; a 2027 recession (Polymarket 35%, Kalshi 24%) and a Fed that is hiking add multiple pressure. Mirrors the 2022-23 drawdown (-40% peak to trough).

base.story: Handset trough in FY27, QTL steady under the renewed Apple licence from Apr 2027, ~$5B FY27 data-center revenue roughly delivered and auto growth continuing; FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$11.2 at ~16-16.5x. Roughly flat from spot, matching the de-trended base-rate median (~0%).

bull.story: Data center tracks the $15B FY29 target with visible Amazon/hyperscaler tranches vesting, memory costs ease in mid-2027 and Android recovers; FY28 EPS ~$12.5 at ~21x, a return to the May-2026 high (~$260).

thesis_break_reason: Around $122 the stock would be back at its 52-week low ($121.99) and ~12x FY27 non-GAAP EPS, at the bottom of its 5-year forward non-GAAP range (10.9x at the Sep-2023 trough). Getting there would most likely mean the ~$5B FY27 data-center ramp failed or slipped badly and/or FY27-28 EPS is heading toward $8.5-9, not ordinary noise. I moved it down from $130 because at ~45-50% vol, $130 (-30%) is roughly a one-sigma annual move.

reasoning: Base rate: from 118 overlapping 12-month windows of QCOM monthly closes (Dec 2015-Sep 2026) the mean 12m log return was +11% (secular up-drift). De-trending that explicitly (subtracting the sample mean) gives 5/25/50/75/95th percentiles of -34%/-18%/-1%/+18%/+55%; overlapping-window sd 0.25 understates today's regime (monthly-implied 39% long-run, 49% last 24 months, 54% realized 1y), so I use a lognormal mixture: 80% at sigma 0.36 and 20% at 0.65 for the stock's history of 40%+ moves. Valuation (corrected per supervisor): I dropped the invalid pairing of GuruFocus's GAAP 10-year median P/E (19.9x) with a blended $9.50 EPS. On a consistent non-GAAP basis ($10.2 FY27 consensus, trimmed to $10.0) QCOM's own history is 11-16x forward and 9-17.6x trailing (median 13.8x), so today's ~18x already embeds a data-center premium. Blending FY28 EPS $11.2 x 16x ($179), the history anchor ($158) and a 5.75% normalized-FCF yield ($183) gives ~$175, a bit below spot and below the supervisor's $185, because I weight QCOM's own non-GAAP multiple history (my lane) more than a mix premium that is still unproven. Offsetting that, equity drift and a Street mean target ~$194 argue against a big negative skew, so I centre the ladder median at ~$183 (P(>=184) 0.49, from 0.53 in round 1). Fed hike verified at the Fed itself (Sep 16, 2026, to 3.75-4.00%). Dilution is negligible (Modular already issued; warrant ~0.5M net). Prediction-market macro odds from round 1 are unchanged (not re-queried). Round-2 research was ~6 queries/fetches.
